text:
### Observed differences

- The order between A26/A27 and the group A35, A36, A41 is reversed. In the earlier window, A35, A36 and A41 each ran before A26 in about 97–100 in 100 traces and before A27 in about 97–100 in 100; in the later window, A26 ran before each of them in about 98 in 100 and A27 before each in about 97–98 in 100. Every pair co-occurs in all 200 traces of both windows, so this is a reordering of activities that are always present, not a change in participation. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015]
- The connections into and out of this group changed accordingly. In the earlier window, about 97 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went to A35 (about 38 in 100), A36 (about 31) or A41 (about 27), and A27 followed A25 about four steps later (lag 4 in 92 in 100); in the later window, about 96 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions go straight to A27 (lag 1 in about 98 in 100). In the earlier window, A26 led almost exclusively to A30 (about 99 in 100, immediately afterwards); in the later window, A26 leads to A35 (about 35 in 100), A36 (about 32) and A41 (about 31), and A30 now follows about four steps after A26 (lag 4 in about 91 in 100). [DIR005, DIR006, LAG002, LAG005, LAG006]
- The group's own exit changed from A27 to A30: in the earlier window, A35, A36 and A41 each led to A27 in roughly 28–36 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, while in the later window A27 is almost never their successor (about 0–1 in 100) and A30 appears at about 30–34 in 100 each, typically one to three steps after A36. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG008]
- Event positions agree: A35, A36 and A41 moved from a mean relative position of about 0.40 to about 0.58 of the trace, while A27 (about 0.46 to 0.39) and A26 (about 0.60 to 0.53) moved slightly earlier; all of these activities still occur in every trace in both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- A02 was largely dropped from the end of the flow. It appeared in about 75 in 100 traces earlier (mean relative position about 0.93, near the end) versus about 21 in 100 later (mean about 0.55), and its co-occurrence with each of A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41, A49 and A50 fell from about 75 in 100 traces to about 21 in 100. [POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- A49 now bypasses A02: in the earlier window, about 72 in 100 of A49's outgoing transitions went to A02 and about 26 to A50, with A50 typically two steps after A49; in the later window, about 83 in 100 go to A50 (immediately, in about 84 in 100) and only about 3 in 100 go to A02. A02's own outgoing transitions, which earlier went to A50 in about 91 in 100 cases (immediately, in about 99 in 100), are later spread thinly over many activities (about 13 in 100 to A50, about 13 to A48, about 11 each to A16 and A15). [DIR011, DIR001, LAG009, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the group of activities A35, A36 and A41 is executed in a different place: earlier it ran between A25 and A27, before both A27 and A26, whereas in the later window A25 leads directly to A27, A26 precedes the group, and A30 is reached only after the group (earlier A25 fed the group, A27 followed it about four steps later, and A30 immediately followed A26). This rests on direct relational evidence — complete order reversals observed in about 97–100 in 100 traces in both windows, with 200 traces behind each pair — corroborated by the matching successor changes at A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41, the lag shifts of A25→A27 and A26→A30, and the position shifts. The screening context also exceeds what a stable process produces: 42 control-flow items qualified against about 0.6 expected by chance across 122 units. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of two pre-existing process variants rather than a modification of a single flow; a few later-window lag profiles (for example A25→A36 and A25→A41) also rest on only two or three observations. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG002, LAG005, POS004, POS005, POS006]

Other differences: In the later window, A02 is largely bypassed at the end of the flow — it appears in about 21 in 100 traces (about 75 in 100 earlier) and A49 leads directly to A50 instead of via A02 — which looks like A02 becoming skippable on the end segment and is not part of the reordering hypothesis above. Smaller redistributions are visible at A47 (share of its outgoing transitions to A48 about 97 in 100 earlier versus 81 in 100 later) and in A06's more varied successors, though the latter rests on only 12 observed outgoing transitions of A06 in the earlier window. [POS001, DIR001, DIR011, LAG009, DIR010, DIR002]
